clue.text: Herb has concern — this isn't the best investment

parts.note: a simple is an old name for a medicinal herb
an interest is a concern, as in a stake in a business

explanation.surface: Someone with a stake in a herb business is warned that it is a poor place for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name, but it is the old word for a medicinal plant. The definition is the whole closing phrase: this kind of return is paid on the principal only, never compounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest paid only on the original sum, with no compounding, earns less than the alternative, so it is a weaker investment.

clue.text: This carries the results of commerce, betraying gamble without question

definitions.text: This carries the results of commerce

parts.note: shopping is slang for informing on someone, betraying them

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word for gamble surrounds the word for question

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A trader's goods are carried by someone who sells out and gambles without hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: BET goes round ASK. 'Shopping' someone is British slang for informing on them.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier for purchases holds the goods a customer buys in a store.

clue.text: Islander blokes accepting cross word reduced by 50%

indicators.note: accepting means the plural word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: blokes are men, read here as two of them, man and man
X is the shape of a cross

indicators.note: reduced by 50% means only the first half of word is kept

explanation.surface: Some men take on a crossword clue cut in half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blokes' gives MAN twice; 'accepting' puts X and WO (half of 'word') between them. A Manx person comes from the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman native to the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea is an inhabitant of that island.

clue.text: See about folk tales?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see, behold
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A reader is told to look up folk stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that folk tales are only one example of traditional knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional beliefs and stories passed down orally make up a people's inherited body of knowledge.

clue.text: See 1
Joke sent up 'a testing process'- but that's not right of marriage

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means the word for joke is read from the bottom

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: a trial is a testing process

explanation.surface: A joke mocks the idea of marriage as a trial, which is not fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns PUN to NUP; 'not right' removes R from TRIAL, leaving TIAL. 'but that's' links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a wedding is relating to marriage, as in nuptial vows.

clue.text: Vital one works, snatching up gold in assessment

indicators.note: snatching means the anagram grabs the next piece and holds it inside
works means the letters are worked into a new order
up in a down clue means the symbol for gold is read upwards

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An essential employee works hard and grabs gold in a performance review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges VITAL ONE into EVALTION; 'snatching' takes UA (AU turned 'up') inside it, after EVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Judging the worth or quality of something is an appraisal.

clue.text: Spare no time in message given to artist

indicators.note: no means the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: a text is a phone message
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone without a moment to spare sends a message to a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no time' drops a T from TEXT, leaving EXT; RA follows ('given to'). RA stands for a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional held in reserve is extra, as in a spare tyre.

clue.text: Naval exercise? Sailor to receive damage, after limiting accomplishment

indicators.note: after means the following piece comes later in the answer

parts.note: tar is a sailor
get means receive

indicators.note: limiting means the word for cost encloses the word for deed

parts.note: damage is slang for cost, as in what's the damage
an act is an accomplishment, a deed

explanation.surface: A sailor in a naval drill takes damage after achieving something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' puts ACT inside PRICE; 'damage' means price, as in 'What's the damage?'. The question mark: firing at a target is just one naval exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting at marked objects for training is one kind of drill a navy runs.

clue.text: Cost of an electric car?

explanation.definitionFit: A fee is a cost, and an electric vehicle runs on stored power topped up at a socket.

clue.text: Whisper on sorting out case of possession

indicators.note: sorting out means putting these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone whispers while tidying a briefcase full of belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorting out' rearranges the nine letters of WHISPER ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding title to something is an instance of possessing it.

clue.text: Feature of church almost entirely black

indicators.note: almost means the word for entirely loses its final letter

parts.note: entirely means all, wholly
tar is black pitch, so black stands for it

explanation.surface: A church fitting is described as nearly all black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last L from ALL, leaving AL, which goes before TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The communion table at the east end is a central fixture of a church interior.

clue.text: Give ear to piano — a minor piece

indicators.note: to means the second piece is attached after the first

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an awn is the bristly beard of an ear of barley, so ear stands loosely for it

explanation.surface: A pianist is told to listen, then plays a short minor-key piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give ear' sounds like 'listen', but it means add AWN (the beard of an ear of grain) to P. 'a minor piece' is the chess sense: the lowest-ranked piece on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: On a chessboard this is the smallest, least valuable unit, so it is a minor chessman.

clue.text: Say lorry with uranium's overdue

parts.note: an artic is an ... lorry, a British term for a truck with a trailer
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
late means overdue

explanation.surface: A truck carrying uranium is running behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the definition, a verb meaning to express in words. ARTIC is British slang for an articulated lorry, a large truck with a hinged trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: To express something clearly in words is to state it, so both mean utter.

clue.text: Slurred company present in pub before "Time!'

indicators.note: before means the pub piece comes ahead of the abbreviation
in means these pieces go inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
here means present

explanation.surface: Drinkers in a pub slur their words just before last orders are called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CO and HERE inside INN; 'before' puts T after it. 'Time!' is the British pub landlord's call that drinking must end.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that is unclear and jumbled, as after drink, is unintelligible.

clue.text: Chosen person's refusal-even I'm taken aback

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: taken aback means the following words are read backwards, as if pushed back

parts.note: even is shortened poetically to e'en
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone selected says no, and even the speaker is startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns round E'EN (poetic 'even') and I'M, giving MINEE after NO. The 's of 'person's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put forward for a post or prize has been selected as a candidate.

clue.text: Newest types of coffee? Time to move on

indicators.note: to move on means one letter is shifted further along the word

parts.note: lattes are milky coffees

explanation.surface: Someone offered the newest kinds of coffee decides it is time to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time to move on' takes one T in LATTES and moves it to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent or up-to-date is the newest.

clue.text: Impure sin? That's misbehaving in a car

indicators.note: misbehaving means these letters act badly and fall out of order

explanation.surface: Impure sin, as in misbehaving in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges IMPURE SIN; 'That's' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hatchback with a compact body is a class of car.

clue.text: See 8 down
Taking steps in eradicating last of grime from part of yard?

indicators.note: eradicating means removing a letter from the phrase that follows

parts.note: a yard is three feet, so one foot is part of it

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of grime is used

explanation.surface: Scrubbing grime from a patch of garden is a matter of getting out there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of yard' looks like a garden but means ONE FOOT, a third of a yard. 'eradicating' removes E, the 'last of' grime, from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Going by walking, rather than riding, is literally moving by steps.

clue.text: Raleigh's discovery another explorer brought up starts to catch on

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the explorer's name is read from the bottom

parts.note: John Cabot was a Venetian explorer who sailed for England

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of catch and on

explanation.surface: What Raleigh found was brought home by another explorer and started to catch on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns CABOT into TOBAC; 'starts to' takes C and O. Sir Walter Raleigh is credited with popularising this in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh is traditionally said to have introduced the smoking leaf to England from the Americas.

clue.text: No work in South-East? Start of ruin for investigator

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of ruin

explanation.surface: With no jobs in South-East England, someone looks into the beginnings of ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts NO and OP inside SE, then R from 'Start of ruin' is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pries into other people's affairs is a kind of investigator.

clue.text: This may contain powder — a way to contain pain?

indicators.note: to contain means the word for road holds the word for pain

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Something holding a powdered painkiller is a way to deal with pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' puts ACHE inside ST; 'a' is a link. The question mark marks the twist on 'contain pain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sealed packet often holds a dose of powder such as a remedy.

clue.text: See 1 down
player with retort

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'player with retort (6,4)': BACK (player) and ANSWER (retort) are there but no definition; the clue appears cut short and no source gives the rest.

clue.text: Sun and light turning up in Middle East country

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday or sun

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word for light is read from the bottom

parts.note: airy means light

explanation.surface: Sunshine and light arrive in a country of the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses AIRY to YRIA after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A state on the eastern Mediterranean coast, capital Damascus, lies in the Middle East.

clue.text: Chap's rage rebounding on college

indicators.note: rebounding means the word for anger bounces back, read in reverse

parts.note: ire is rage

explanation.surface: A man's fury bounces back onto his college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebounding' turns IRE round to ERI; C (college) follows. The 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name stands for a chap in crosswords: any male given name fits the definition.

clue.text: One has to leave Italian city -go

indicators.note: has to leave means the Roman numeral for one departs from the city's name

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone must leave an Italian city and go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to leave' takes I (one) out of TURIN. 'go' is a noun here, a go in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A go in a game is someone's chance to play, a spell or shot.

clue.text: King's year that is represented in part of Mass

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
year gives YR

explanation.surface: A king's year is commemorated in a section of the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is represented in' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kyrie eleison, 'Lord have mercy', is an opening prayer sung in the Mass liturgy.

clue.text: Core of Schubert transformed in one Italian composer

indicators.note: transformed means the remaining letters are rearranged
core of means the word without its outer letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Part of a Schubert work is reworked in the style of an Italian composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Core of' strips S and T from Schubert, leaving CHUBER; 'transformed' rearranges it to CHERUB, then IN and I follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Cherubini was an Italian-born composer of operas and sacred music.

clue.text: Machine containing tree splinters

indicators.note: splinters means the words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A machine holds a tree that is being chopped into splinters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splinters' is a verb here, breaking CONTAINING TREE into fourteen letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam-powered vehicle for hauling heavy loads is a machine.
